title: Two families of older cards
headline: Two families explain a quarter of the older cards that rose.
dek: Since Oct 13, 47 of the 172 rows where an older-set card rose on the board's 7-day list came from two printing families: 30 from cards named Cracked Ice Holo (12 cards, from the Deck Exclusives and Miscellaneous sets) and 17 from the Prize Pack Series set (6 cards). They are 18 of the 85 different older cards that rose, so they repeat: the same few cards keep coming back. The Cracked Ice Holo run peaked on Oct 27 to Nov 2 with 16 rows in the week, and the last Cracked Ice Holo rise on the 7-day list was Nov 6; the Prize Pack run had 10 rows in the week of Nov 3, and its last rise was Nov 8. Every one is unconfirmed.
why_now: Tuesday's File said the new sets fall and the old cards rise, and could not say why. A quarter of those rises are two families of printings, which is a smaller thing to look at than "old cards", and both runs have faded, so this is the week to look before they are gone from the lists.
risk: A card leaving the 7-day list does not mean its price fell: it may have moved under 5%, stopped changing, or stopped trading often enough to qualify, and we only see a card's price while it is listed. The last readings here are from the week they were last listed. Eighteen cards is a small group, and the rises are 19.5% to 50.6% in a week on thin markets, each from one reading. What the two families have in common isn't visible in price data. No sale was checked behind any of it. This is not a read on whether these prices are high or low.
what_to_watch: Whether any Cracked Ice Holo or Prize Pack Series card makes the 7-day list again (the latest was Sylveon - 72/111 and Alolan Vulpix V, on the since-yesterday list on Nov 10 and Nov 12). Whether the next family shows up the same way: a handful of cards from one printing run repeating for two weeks. And the label: the morning one of these cards has a checked sale, its row stops reading Unconfirmed.
source: TCGplayer market prices via tcgcsv.com, from the board's published lists, Oct 13 to Nov 14, 2026 (33 mornings)

foot: Market price: TCGplayer's average of recent completed sales of the same card, condition and printing (help.tcgplayer.com). The counts: the board's own published 7-day lists, Oct 13 to Nov 14, 2026, 33 mornings (git history of data/movers.json). "Older" means a set whose name does not begin ME; a rise is a 7-day row with a positive change. 172 such rows in all. "Cracked Ice Holo": cards whose published name contains it: 30 rows, 12 cards (Umbreon 10/90, Pikachu 35/108, Dragonite 151/236, Entei 4/132, Metagross 4/95, Typhlosion 32/123, Gyarados 4/123, Minccino BW13, Charizard 25/185, Mewtwo 51/108, Blastoise 25/181, Charizard 1/99), all up. "Prize Pack Series": cards from the Prize Pack Series Cards set: 17 rows, 6 cards (Boltund VMAX 104/264, Pumpkaboo 076/203, Suicune V 031/203, Lugia VSTAR 139/195, Charizard VSTAR 018/172, Blaziken V 020/198), all up. 30 + 17 = 47 of 172 is 27%; 18 of 85 different older cards is 21%. A card counts once per morning it was listed. The table: three of the 18 cards at their last 7-day list appearance (readings Oct 29, Nov 3 and Nov 4); start-of-week prices are worked back from the listed price and its rounded change, so within a dollar. The list: up to 10 Pokémon cards worth $20 or more that moved 5% or more in a week; with no checked sales, a move shows only if it's 60% or less, the lowest listing moved the same way by at least a quarter as much, the price changed in the last 2 days, and the card trades. Unconfirmed: no sale checked by Mission Control's Sale Integrity Layer in that window. Not advice.
